❯ In ONE single assistant message, with no text before the tool calls, issue three Write tool calls in parallel: cache.js (an LRU cache class, about 70 lines), queu…
   72
   73 - **`Store`** keeps values with an optional time-to-live. Expired entries are removed lazily when read and also by a periodic sweep whose timer is `unref()`e
      d so it never keeps the process alive; call `close()` to stop the sweep explicitly in tests.
   74 - **`LRUCache`** evicts the least recently used entry once it is full and can call an `onEvict(key, value)` hook. `stats()` reports size, hits, misses, and h
      it rate.
   75 - **`JobQueue`** runs async jobs up to a concurrency limit and retries failures with exponential backoff capped at `maxBackoffMs`. `add(fn)` returns a promis
      e for the job's result, and the queue emits `queued`, `retry`, `done`, `failed`, and `idle` events.
   76 - **`RateLimiter`** keeps one token bucket per key with an upper bound on how many keys it tracks. `check(key)` returns `{ allowed, remaining, retryAfterMs }
      `, which maps directly onto a `429` response with a `Retry-After` header.
   77 - **`Logger`** writes one line per record in text or JSON, filters by level, and supports child loggers that carry extra fields. The default instance reads `
      LOG_LEVEL` and `LOG_FORMAT` from the environment.
   78 - **`validate.js`** offers composable checks such as `v.object`, `v.string`, and `v.array`; `parseAndValidate(schema, raw)` parses JSON and returns `{ ok, er
      rors, body }` with path-qualified error messages like `body.name: is required`.
   79 - **`Emitter`** in `events.js` is a lightweight alternative to Node's `EventEmitter` with `on`, `once`, `off`, and `emit`, where a throwing listener is repor
      ted through an `error` event instead of stopping the remaining listeners from running.
   80
   81 ## Error format
   82
   83 Every error response is a JSON object with an `error` string and, where useful, extra context fields such as `path`, `method`, `limit`, or `id`. Clients shou
      ld branch on the HTTP status code first and treat the `error` text as a human-readable message rather than a stable machine identifier, because the wording m
      ay change (as it already has once, when the 404 message became `no such route`).
   84
   85 ## Limits
   86
   87 - Request bodies: 1 KB for both `/echo` and `/users`.
   88 - Users: unbounded in memory; there is no pagination on `GET /users`.
   89 - No authentication, TLS, or CORS handling is built in.
   90
   91 ## Development
   92
   93 Check a module's syntax without running it:
   94
   95 ```sh
   96 node --check routes.js
   97 ```
   98
